title: Elements: A River Worth Returning To
premise: Starting from four storybook elements, travel from an orchard to a coastal gathering. Make useful things for people you meet. The world remembers what you leave behind.

items.label: Earth
items.description: Loose ground: mineral grit, clay and the material in which roots grow.

items.label: Water
items.description: Flowing, soaking and carrying; a liquid that takes the shape of its container.

items.label: Air
items.description: The invisible moving world around us. It carries moisture and feeds a flame.

items.label: Fire
items.description: Heat and light. It cooks, hardens and changes materials rather than merely joining them.

items.label: Clay
items.description: Soft, fine earth that holds an impressed shape while wet.

items.label: Stone
items.description: Hard, rough mineral material; its weight and abrasive surfaces can do work.

items.label: Bowl
items.description: An open, hollow vessel with a broad mouth and a stable base.

items.label: Brick
items.description: A hard, regular block of fired clay, made for stacking into lasting structures.

items.label: Rain
items.description: Water arriving from the sky, enough to soak the ground rather than fill a vessel neatly.

items.label: Plant
items.description: A living stem with roots and leaves; a source of several different natural materials.

items.label: Grain
items.description: Dry edible seeds with a tough outer surface and a starchy interior.

items.label: Flour
items.description: Fine meal ground from grain. Loose and powdery until it is wetted.

items.label: Dough
items.description: A soft mass of flour and water. It can hold its shape, but has not yet risen or baked.

items.label: Flatbread
items.description: A simple cooked bread without a raised, airy crumb.

items.label: Fruit
items.description: Ripe, juicy produce with flesh around its seeds.

items.label: Fruit juice
items.description: The fruit's liquid, separated from its flesh; sweet enough to feed fermentation.

items.label: Sand
items.description: Small, hard mineral grains. Loose when poured, abrasive when rubbed.

items.label: Glass
items.description: A hard, clear material that lets light through but needs shaping to give it a particular job.

items.label: Wood
items.description: Rough timber: solid lengths with grain and bulk, not flat boards yet.

items.label: Window
items.description: A pane held in a wooden frame, admitting light while closing an opening.

items.label: Plant fiber
items.description: Loose strands from plant stems. Flexible, but not yet organized into a strong length or sheet.

items.label: Thread
items.description: A long, fine strand spun from fibers; useful for binding and stitching.

items.label: Cloth
items.description: A flexible sheet made from interlaced threads.

items.label: Rope
items.description: Thicker cordage that can hold a load or keep larger pieces together.

items.label: Sleeping mat
items.description: A padded woven surface that separates a sleeper from the cold ground.

items.label: House
items.description: A small weatherproof home with solid walls and a timber roof. Its dark interior would benefit from a fitted window.

items.label: Axe
items.description: A sharp stone edge on a handle. Its job is to cut and shape wood, not to pound it.

items.label: Planks
items.description: Flat, cut boards with broad faces and straight edges; easier to join into surfaces than rough timber.

items.label: Footbridge
items.description: A narrow deck spanning the brook, supported and held together above the water.

items.label: Wheel
items.description: A solid wooden disc, shaped to roll or turn around its centre. Its rim is still smooth.

items.label: Wheelset
items.description: Wheels mounted on a wooden axle: a rolling undercarriage, not yet a load-carrying body.

items.label: Handcart
items.description: A small rolling platform for moving a load by hand.

items.label: Waterwheel
items.description: A paddled wheel that moving water can turn. Its turning force still needs a connection to useful work.

items.label: Millstone
items.description: A heavy circular grinding stone. It can crush grain, but will not turn by itself.

items.label: Wooden gear
items.description: A wooden wheel with teeth cut around its rim, able to pass rotation to another mechanism.

items.label: Mill gearing
items.description: A connected drive taking rotation from the waterwheel toward the grinding machinery.

items.label: Grain mill
items.description: A water-driven grinding machine built for the village's daily grain, not just a single handful.

items.label: Sack
items.description: A stitched cloth bag, closed at the sides and open at the top.

items.label: Flour sack
items.description: A sack filled with flour, ready to take to the baker.

items.label: Wild starter
items.description: A living flour culture. Given moisture and time, it makes gas and changes dough.

items.label: Risen dough
items.description: Dough expanded by fermentation, with small bubbles held inside it.

items.label: Bread
items.description: A baked loaf with an airy crumb and a firm crust.

items.label: Basket
items.description: A light woven carrier with enough shape to hold its contents together.

items.label: Picnic basket
items.description: A basket packed with bread for a journey.

items.label: Jam
items.description: Fruit cooked down into a thick spread; it still needs a vessel for keeping.

items.label: Jar
items.description: A hollow clay container with a narrower opening than a bowl.

items.label: Jar lid
items.description: A fitted wooden cover for the mouth of a jar.

items.label: Preserve jar
items.description: A jar filled with fruit preserve, but not yet covered.

items.label: Sealed preserves
items.description: Fruit preserve put away in a covered jar for later meals.

items.label: Cider
items.description: A fermented fruit drink, no longer the fresh juice it began as.

items.label: Glaze
items.description: A mineral coating for pottery; its finished surface depends on the potter's firing.

items.label: Glazed bottle
items.description: A narrow-necked ceramic vessel with a finished, glazed surface.

items.label: Cider bottle
items.description: A closed vessel of cider, ready to carry without spilling.

items.label: Kiln
items.description: An enclosed firing chamber that concentrates heat around pottery or other materials.

items.label: Tile
items.description: A flat, regular piece of shaped clay for covering a surface.

items.label: Glazed bowl
items.description: A fired bowl with a smooth, finished surface rather than bare porous clay.

items.label: Table
items.description: A sturdy raised wooden surface for preparing, displaying or serving things.

items.label: Tiled table
items.description: A table with a durable tiled top, easy to wipe after a shared meal.

items.label: Hammerstone
items.description: A rounded hand-held cobble with a blunt striking face; made for pounding rather than cutting.

items.label: Iron ore
items.description: Rock containing iron-bearing minerals, not usable metal yet.

items.label: Bellows
items.description: A flexible air chamber that pushes a directed flow into a fire.

items.label: Forge
items.description: A hot working hearth with a forced air supply for metalworking.

items.label: Iron
items.description: Workable metal: strong enough for edges, fasteners and fittings once shaped.

items.label: Pickaxe
items.description: A pointed metal head on a handle, suited to breaking hard ground and rock.

items.label: Carving tool
items.description: A sharpened metal cutting tool for careful shaping rather than broad chopping.

items.label: Nails
items.description: Pointed metal fasteners; their stems can also serve as small pins.

items.label: Hinge
items.description: Two metal leaves joined around a pin so one side can swing relative to the other.

items.label: Wooden chest
items.description: A box assembled from boards, with room to protect things inside.

items.label: Tool chest
items.description: A wooden chest with a hinged lid, keeping shared tools together.

items.label: Raft
items.description: Timbers bound into a floating platform, without a sail.

items.label: Sail
items.description: A broad sheet rigged to catch the wind and pull on its lines.

items.label: Sailboat
items.description: A small floating craft able to use the wind for movement.

items.label: Pier post
items.description: A stout prepared post, ready to support a landing above the water.

items.label: Dock
items.description: A fixed landing where a boat can meet the shore.

items.label: Charcoal
items.description: A dark, carbon-rich material made from wood under controlled firing.

items.label: Torch
items.description: A hand-held source of flame and light on a wooden support.

items.label: Lantern
items.description: A light protected by a clear enclosure rather than left as an exposed flame.

items.label: Tower
items.description: A tall masonry structure with an opening to look out from above its surroundings.

items.label: Lighthouse
items.description: A high harbour light that can be seen from the water.

items.label: Float
items.description: A buoyant, sealed object that stays on the water's surface.

items.label: Mooring buoy
items.description: A floating marker with a line to hold a boat in place.

items.label: Seeds
items.description: Small beginnings for new plants, gathered from mature growth.

items.label: Seedlings
items.description: Young growing plants, still tender and in need of support or shelter.

items.label: Trellis
items.description: An open framework of stretched lines, giving climbing stems something to grip.

items.label: Climbing garden
items.description: Young plants trained up a trellis rather than left to trail on the ground.

items.label: Greenhouse
items.description: A light-filled shelter protecting tender plants from the weather.

items.label: Saw
items.description: A toothed metal edge for cutting wood along a controlled line.

items.label: Hollow pipe
items.description: A wooden conduit with an open passage through its length.

items.label: Pump
items.description: A mechanism for lifting or moving water; its moving parts still need power.

items.label: Water pump
items.description: A pump coupled to a waterwheel, using the stream's motion to lift water.

items.label: Reservoir
items.description: A lined storage basin, ready to hold a supply of water.

items.label: Filled reservoir
items.description: A storage basin supplied by the pump rather than carried buckets.

items.label: Water channel
items.description: A supported waterway directing flow along a planned route.

items.label: Irrigation channel
items.description: A channel connected to the stored water supply.

items.label: Irrigated garden
items.description: The climbing garden with water delivered to its beds.

items.label: Flowers
items.description: The colourful blossoms of a living plant.

items.label: Dye
items.description: Colour extracted into a liquid, able to stain absorbent material.

items.label: Dyed cloth
items.description: Cloth that has taken up colour through its fibers.

items.label: Loom
items.description: A frame that holds threads under tension so they can be woven in order.

items.label: Patterned cloth
items.description: Woven cloth with a deliberate arrangement of colours.

items.label: Festival banner
items.description: A patterned flag on a support, visible above the crowd.

items.label: Awning
items.description: Cloth stretched over a supporting frame to give shade.

items.label: Canopy
items.description: A supported and tied covering sheltering a larger open space.

items.label: Paper pulp
items.description: Wet, separated plant fibers suspended in water.

items.label: Paper
items.description: A thin, dry sheet of joined fibers; a surface for marks and records.

items.label: Ink
items.description: Dark liquid pigment that leaves a readable mark on a light surface.

items.label: Printing block
items.description: A wooden face carved with a design that can be repeated.

items.label: Inked printing block
items.description: A printing face coated with ink on its raised surfaces.

items.label: Printed invitations
items.description: Repeated printed notices inviting people to the river gathering.

items.label: Letter
items.description: A written message that can travel separately from its author.

items.label: Mailboat
items.description: A boat carrying written messages between settlements.

items.label: Hollow tube
items.description: A small wooden tube with an open interior, ready to carry air or hold aligned parts.

items.label: Flute
items.description: A hollow wind instrument whose vibrating air makes a note.

items.label: Drum
items.description: A stretched surface over a hollow body, resonating when struck.

items.label: Platform
items.description: A flat, supported deck raised above the ground.

items.label: Bandstand
items.description: A sheltered raised place where musicians can gather and be heard.

items.label: Puppet
items.description: A small figure made to be moved while telling a story.

items.label: Curtain
items.description: Hanging cloth that can cover or reveal an opening.

items.label: Stage
items.description: A raised performance space with a curtain to reveal the action.

items.label: Puppet theatre
items.description: A little performance stage built around moving figures and their stories.

items.label: Paint
items.description: A prepared coloured medium that can cover a surface with visible shapes.

items.label: Brush
items.description: Flexible fibers gathered at the end of a small handle for applying colour.

items.label: Picture
items.description: A deliberately painted image, not merely a blank sheet or a pot of colour.

items.label: Bound book
items.description: A stack of pages held together along one edge, ready to preserve a sequence.

items.label: Picture book
items.description: A bound sequence of images that can tell a story after the storyteller leaves.

items.label: Lens
items.description: A shaped, polished piece of glass that bends light.

items.label: Magnifier
items.description: A lens held in a frame for examining nearby small details.

items.label: Telescope
items.description: Lenses aligned in a tube for viewing things that are far away.

items.label: Microscope
items.description: An arrangement of magnifying optics for seeing very small nearby details.

items.label: Glass slide
items.description: A small flat piece of clear glass that can support a thin sample.

items.label: Pond water
items.description: A collected drop from the still pond, with more in it than the eye first sees.

items.label: Pond slide
items.description: A thin pond-water sample supported on clear glass for close examination.

items.label: Pressed plant specimen
items.description: A flattened, preserved plant sample retaining its visible form.

items.label: Herbarium
items.description: A bound collection of preserved plant specimens with room for their records.

items.label: Leaf study
items.description: An observed account of a leaf's small structures, seen through a lens.

items.label: Botanical drawing
items.description: A recorded plant study showing the features an observer noticed.

items.label: Illustrated flora
items.description: A guide joining preserved specimens to drawings of their distinguishing features.

items.label: Measuring jar
items.description: A vessel with a marked scale, making amounts comparable rather than guessed.

items.label: Rain gauge
items.description: A marked collector showing how much rain has fallen.

items.label: Windsock
items.description: A light fabric tube that turns and extends with the wind.

items.label: Rain record

items.label: Weather record

items.label: Net

items.label: Fish
items.description: A catch brought from the shore, still in need of preparation for keeping.

items.label: Brine

items.label: Salt

items.label: Smoke

items.label: Smoked fish
items.description: Fish prepared with smoke for the journey; represented here without a real preservation procedure.

items.label: Vinegar

items.label: Pickles

items.label: Pickle jar
items.description: A container holding the prepared pickles for transport.

items.label: Filter bed

items.label: Water filter
items.description: A filter bed held in a conduit so water can pass through it.

items.label: Filtered water

items.label: Boiled water

items.label: Drinking-water bowl
items.description: A serving bowl of the water prepared for this fictional gathering.

items.label: Covered urn
items.description: A large ceramic vessel with a fitted cover, protecting what is put inside.

items.label: Drinking-water urn
items.description: The gathering's prepared water in a covered serving vessel.

items.label: Washstand
items.description: A basin held at a comfortable height for washing.

items.label: Grain bin
items.description: A substantial wooden store for dry grain.

items.label: Drying rack
items.description: An open frame and mesh allowing air to reach food from several sides.

items.label: Dried fruit
items.description: Fruit from which much of the moisture has been removed.

items.label: Crock
items.description: A thick-walled clay storage vessel, sturdier than the small jar.

items.label: Sealed crock
items.description: A storage crock fitted with its cover.

items.label: Fruit crock
items.description: A covered crock holding dried fruit for later meals.

items.label: Seed oil
items.description: Liquid pressed from seeds, able to carry energy and feed a wick.

items.label: Wick
items.description: Absorbent fibers carrying oil toward a flame.

items.label: Oil lamp
items.description: A small vessel holding oil and a wick for a steady light.

items.label: Watch lamp
items.description: An oil light protected by glass for the night watch.

items.label: Paper lantern frame
items.description: A light wooden framework covered in paper, awaiting its source of light.

items.label: Paper lantern
items.description: A small light enclosed in a paper-covered frame.

items.label: Floating lantern
items.description: A lantern supported upright on a buoyant base.

items.label: Hourglass
items.description: Sand passing through a narrow opening to mark an interval.

items.label: Pendulum
items.description: A suspended weight that swings back and forth with a regular rhythm.

items.label: Clockwork
items.description: A powered, regulated train of moving parts; much more than a freely spinning wheel.

items.label: Clock
items.description: A housed timekeeping mechanism with a readable indication of time.

items.label: Ferry timetable
items.description: A written timetable relating departure times to stops on the river.

items.label: Bell
items.description: A hollow metal body shaped to ring when struck.

items.label: Dinner bell
items.description: A bell hung with a pull line, ready to call people together.

items.label: Star chart
items.description: A drawn record of the stars' positions, used to recognize the sky.

items.label: Tripod
items.description: A three-legged support that holds an instrument steadily above the ground.

items.label: Mounted telescope
items.description: A telescope on a stable stand, keeping the view steady.

items.label: Crossing map
items.description: A portable record of the brook crossing, so the bridge itself can stay where it belongs.

items.label: River map
items.description: A record linking the crossing and boat landing along the river.

items.label: Harbour map
items.description: The river map extended to include the harbour's light and approach.

items.label: Navigation chart
items.description: A route record joined to the night sky, for someone who has not made this journey before.

items.label: Arch
items.description: A curved masonry span carrying weight around an opening.

items.label: Arcade
items.description: A covered walkway built around an open masonry span.

items.label: Gallery
items.description: A sheltered public space displaying pictures for people to see together.

items.label: Exhibition catalogue
items.description: A portable record of the images displayed in the gallery.

items.label: Mosaic pieces
items.description: Small pieces of coloured glass prepared to be arranged into an image.

items.label: Mosaic
items.description: An image assembled from small pieces held in a clay bed.

items.label: Ash

items.label: Lye

items.label: Soap
items.description: A washing material formed from fats or oils and alkali; no real making procedure is provided here.

items.label: Wash station
items.description: A washstand supplied with soap for the people preparing the meal.

items.label: Stove
items.description: An enclosed cooking structure with a durable metal heating surface.

items.label: Cooking pot
items.description: A heat-resistant vessel with a broad opening for stirring food as it cooks.

items.label: Porridge
items.description: Grain cooked into a warm, soft meal.

items.label: Fruit compote
items.description: Fruit softened by cooking into a spoonable dish.

items.label: Feast
items.description: Bread and fruit prepared as a meal to share.

items.label: Feast table
items.description: The communal table laid with food, ready for guests.

items.label: Weather book
items.description: A bound record preserving the season's observations of wind and rain.

items.label: River atlas
items.description: A durable account of the route and its changing weather, left for future travellers.

locations.description: An open view above the harbour.

recipes.description: A blunt cobble for striking, rather than a cutting edge.

recipes.description: Metal leaves joined around a pin can swing while remaining connected.

stages.title: Four beginnings
stages.speaker: The keeper
stages.motivation: The river gathering is a month away. We begin with earth, water, air and fire. Make a bowl for supper and bricks for a hearth.

area.label: Four beginnings
area.travelText: Our next stop: Four beginnings. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: A bowl to eat from and bricks to build with—not bad for four beginnings. Now we need something worth putting in that bowl.

stages.title: The first supper
stages.speaker: The baker
stages.motivation: Bring our useful things to the orchard. Bake flatbread and pour fruit juice; we have a long walk tomorrow.

area.label: The first supper
area.travelText: Our next stop: The first supper. We’re taking what we need with us; the things we leave stay here.

stages.completionText: Flatbread and juice: a proper first supper. Take your time; we can look for somewhere to rest before the next stretch of river.

stages.title: A place to wake up
stages.speaker: The neighbour
stages.motivation: The orchard path ends at my unfinished cottage. Fit it with a window, and make a sleeping mat before nightfall.

area.label: A place to wake up
area.travelText: Our next stop: A place to wake up. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

objectives.text: Fit a window into the house.

stages.completionText: Daylight through the window, and a mat for the night: thank you, the cottage feels like a home now. The brook is just beyond the orchard.

stages.title: Across the brook
stages.speaker: The carpenter
stages.motivation: Our neighbours are gathering downstream. Give this village a footbridge and a handcart for its heavy loads. Record this part of the river on a map before we leave.

area.label: Across the brook
area.travelText: Our next stop: Across the brook. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: A bridge for our feet, a cart for our loads, and a map for the next traveller. Downstream, the miller has been watching that same water go to waste.

stages.title: The mill bend
stages.speaker: The miller
stages.motivation: You have ground a handful by hand. Now let the stream do the village’s grinding: get its turning motion to the stone, then fill a flour sack. The baker has promised you a different kind of loaf.

area.label: The mill bend
area.travelText: Our next stop: The mill bend. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: You could grind a handful before; now the village has a mill to do the work. Take that flour sack to the baker—she has a lighter loaf in mind.

stages.title: Bread for the journey
stages.speaker: The baker
stages.motivation: You have given the village flour without aching arms. Come to my warm cellar: I want to send you off with a loaf that is light inside, and a picnic basket for the road.

area.label: Bread for the journey
area.travelText: Our next stop: Bread for the journey. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: There it is: a loaf with air in its crumb, and a basket for the road. The orchard keeper has been wondering how to save a little summer for the gathering.

stages.title: Keep the summer
stages.speaker: The orchard keeper
stages.motivation: The fruit will not stay ripe until the gathering. Make sealed preserves and a bottle of cider to send ahead.

area.label: Keep the summer
area.travelText: Our next stop: Keep the summer. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: Preserves under a lid and cider in a bottle. We can bring something of this orchard to the gathering without asking the fruit to stay ripe forever.

stages.title: The potters yard
stages.speaker: The potter
stages.motivation: The gathering needs a table that will survive a thousand suppers. Build a kiln and finish a glazed bowl and tiled tabletop.

area.label: The potters yard
area.travelText: Our next stop: The potters yard. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: A smooth bowl and a table made for many suppers. Useful things can be beautiful, too. Our neighbours at the quarry could use a little of your ingenuity.

stages.title: Tools to lend
stages.speaker: The smith
stages.motivation: My quarry contains a red ore, but bare hands will not bring it out. Leave me a pickaxe and a hinged tool chest for anyone who needs them.

area.label: Tools to lend
area.travelText: Our next stop: Tools to lend. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: A pickaxe for hard ground and a chest to keep our tools together. Leave them within reach of the next pair of hands; there is wider water ahead.

stages.title: A river wide enough
stages.speaker: The ferryman
stages.motivation: The next village is across open water. Make a landing and a sailboat; the handcart can stay with the bridge. Record this part of the river on a map before we leave.

area.label: A river wide enough
area.travelText: Our next stop: A river wide enough. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: A landing, a sailboat, and another stretch added to the map. The river is beginning to join our villages instead of keeping them apart.

stages.title: A light to come home to
stages.speaker: The harbour keeper
stages.motivation: Visitors will arrive after dark. Build a lighthouse on this headland and a mooring buoy below it. Record this part of the river on a map before we leave.

area.label: A light to come home to
area.travelText: Our next stop: A light to come home to. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: A light above the water, a buoy below it, and a harbour marked on the map. Now let us think about the people those boats will bring.

stages.title: The walled garden
stages.speaker: The gardener
stages.motivation: We can feed the guests without emptying the orchard. Give the climbing plants a trellis, and make a greenhouse for the young seedlings.

area.label: Orchard garden
area.travelText: Our next stop: The walled garden. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: The climbing plants have support, and the tender ones have shelter. We have made them a good beginning; those uphill beds still need water.

stages.title: Water without the climb
stages.speaker: The gardener
stages.motivation: The beds are uphill. Build a pump and a small reservoir, then bring water through an irrigation channel.

area.label: Orchard garden
area.travelText: Our next stop: Water without the climb. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: Water reaches the garden without another climb with a bucket. That leaves more hands free to prepare a welcome for our guests.

stages.title: A welcome in colour
stages.speaker: The weaver
stages.motivation: Our guests should see the hall from the river. Make a bright banner and a canopy where they can sit out of the sun.

area.label: A welcome in colour
area.travelText: Our next stop: A welcome in colour. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: A banner to find us by and a canopy to gather beneath—it looks like a welcome. Now we ought to send the invitation.

stages.title: News before the boats
stages.speaker: The messenger
stages.motivation: People cannot come to a gathering they have never heard of. Print invitations and fit a mailboat to carry them upriver.

area.label: News before the boats
area.travelText: Our next stop: News before the boats. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: The invitations are printed and the mailboat is ready. We have something to tell our neighbours—and soon we will need something for them to hear.

stages.title: A tune in the square
stages.speaker: The musician
stages.motivation: We have a date and an audience. Make a flute and a drum, then a little bandstand where the players can hear one another.

area.label: Village square
area.travelText: Our next stop: A tune in the square. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: A flute, a drum, and a place for the players. That is the beginning of a fine gathering. Leave a little room for the storyteller.

stages.title: A story to pass on
stages.speaker: The storyteller
stages.motivation: The children know the river better than its stories. Make a puppet theatre and a picture book about this journey.

area.label: Village square
area.travelText: Our next stop: A story to pass on. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: A little theatre for moving stories, and a picture book for keeping them. There are other stories nearby, too—even in a drop from the pond.

stages.title: What the water hides
stages.speaker: The naturalist
stages.motivation: There is a whole country in a drop of pond water. Make a microscope and a clear slide so we can show it at the gathering.

area.label: What the water hides
area.travelText: Our next stop: What the water hides. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: A pond sample and the means to look closely. We need not travel far to find something unfamiliar; let us look at the plants along this same river.

stages.title: Names for the green world
stages.speaker: The naturalist
stages.motivation: Our visitors keep asking which plants belong to this river. Make an illustrated flora, with a pressed specimen and a drawing they can compare.

area.label: Names for the green world
area.travelText: Our next stop: Names for the green world. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: Specimens and drawings, together in a flora we can share. A traveller can compare a leaf with the page instead of relying on our memories.

stages.title: A promise to the sky
stages.speaker: The boatbuilder
stages.motivation: We should not invite small boats out blindly. Make a rain gauge, a windsock and a weather record for the harbour wall.

area.label: A promise to the sky
area.travelText: Our next stop: A promise to the sky. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: We have a record of wind and rain, not just a guess at the sky. I will keep it with our preparations; the shore cook is planning the crossing meals.

stages.title: Food for the crossing
stages.speaker: The shore cook
stages.motivation: There is no hearth on the crossing. Make smoked fish and a jar of pickles for the boats, not just another pretty table.

area.label: Food for the crossing
area.travelText: Our next stop: Food for the crossing. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: Smoked fish and a jar of pickles: provisions for a boat without a hearth. The guests on shore will need looking after as well.

stages.title: Water for everyone
stages.speaker: The host
stages.motivation: When the guests arrive, a clean washstand and safe water matter more than decorations. Make a washstand and a covered drinking-water urn.

area.label: Water for everyone
area.travelText: Our next stop: Water for everyone. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: The washstand and covered water urn are ready. A welcome is more than decoration; it is noticing what people will need when they arrive.

stages.title: The cellar before winter
stages.speaker: The storekeeper
stages.motivation: The gathering should leave us ready for winter, not poorer. Build a grain bin and drying rack, and store dried fruit in a sealed crock.

area.label: The cellar before winter
area.travelText: Our next stop: The cellar before winter. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: Room for grain, and dried fruit put away in its crock. We can celebrate the season without forgetting the one that follows it.

stages.title: Lights on the water
stages.speaker: The lantern maker
stages.motivation: At dusk we will send lights down the river. Make floating lanterns that stay upright, and a lamp for the night watch.

area.label: Lights on the water
area.travelText: Our next stop: Lights on the water. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: A light that can float and a lamp for the watch. Keep the floating lantern for our sheltered landing; first, let us agree when everyone should arrive.

stages.title: When the boats arrive
stages.speaker: The harbour keeper
stages.motivation: A gathering needs a time as well as a place. Make a ferry timetable and a bell to call everyone in.

area.label: When the boats arrive
area.travelText: Our next stop: When the boats arrive. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: A timetable for the boats and a bell to call us together. The last visitors will come after dark; the watcher has been studying their route.

stages.title: A route through the night
stages.speaker: The watcher
stages.motivation: The last boats will come after dark. Make a mounted telescope and a star chart, then join our river records into a navigation chart for the visitors.

area.label: Above the headland
area.travelText: Our next stop: Above the headland. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: River landmarks and stars on one navigation chart, with a steady telescope beside it. We can leave the next traveller something better than vague directions.

stages.title: A roof for the pictures
stages.speaker: The artist
stages.motivation: The stories deserve a dry wall, not just a page in a trunk. Make a covered gallery, a mosaic and an exhibition catalogue.

area.label: A roof for the pictures
area.travelText: Our next stop: A roof for the pictures. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: A mosaic on display and a catalogue to carry away. Our gathering has things to look at as well as things to eat; the kitchen is nearly ready for us.

stages.title: Before the great cooking
stages.speaker: The host
stages.motivation: We have water now. Make soap and a wash station beside the kitchen, so the cooks can clean their hands.

area.label: Before the great cooking
area.travelText: Our next stop: Before the great cooking. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: Soap at the washstand, where the cooks can use it. Now we can turn from preparing the kitchen to preparing the meal.

stages.title: A kitchen for the crowd
stages.speaker: The cook
stages.motivation: Cold provisions are for the boats. Here on shore, build a stove and cook porridge and fruit compote for the early arrivals.

area.label: A kitchen for the crowd
area.travelText: Our next stop: A kitchen for the crowd. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

stages.completionText: The stove is ready, with porridge and fruit compote for the early arrivals. Bring the gathering to the table; we have been preparing for this together.

stages.title: A river worth returning to
stages.speaker: The keeper
stages.motivation: Everyone has brought something. Set a feast and finish the river atlas. Float a lantern in the sheltered basin at this landing.

area.label: A river worth returning to
area.travelText: Our next stop: A river worth returning to. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

objectives.text: Place the floating lantern at the gathering landing.

stages.completionText: The table is laid, the atlas is finished, and a lantern floats at our landing. From four beginnings, a river full of things to share. Come and sit with us.

notes: Storybook alchemy, not a chemistry or survival instruction manual. A recipe denotes a recognisable craft relationship, not a physically complete bill of materials.
First design pass. Recipe count is not evidence of game length or fun. Exact required closure and playtester reports are separate evidence.
No choose-N goals, invisible benches, automatic terminal hiding, inventory scarcity or forced timer.
Uses v3 current-scene packing: only the existing prerequisite frontier is brought along; things left behind remain tangible at prior places.

v4 adds concrete material/function descriptions, names the wheeled undercarriage Wheelset, fixes hinge and hammerstone relationships, and folds the one-creation map synthesis into the night-navigation chapter. No quota recipes added.

v5 responds to the full-v4 stop: natural alternate routes retain canonical outputs; fitting the house window now satisfies the actual shelter goal; mill and baker acknowledge prior flour and offer a concrete next reward. No new item or quota recipe added.

checkpoints.label: 11. A light to come home to
